$comment: The docs on the site (/docs/), built from these files by frontend/plugins/docsSite.ts. `pages` lists the pages; `source` is relative to this folder. The previous / next links follow the sidebar (`nav`) order. Every page needs a stub at frontend/docs/<slug>/index.html (the docs home: frontend/docs/index.html). `nav` is the sidebar: an item names a page (with an optional anchor), or an `href` from the site root or an absolute URL.

pages.title: Why Proschi
pages.description: What Proschi is for: architecture diagrams as text, request flows you can play, and designs checked by a simulation in your browser.

pages.title: Quickstart
pages.description: Your first Proschi diagram in two minutes: services, a request flow, a failure, and a requirement that checks itself.

pages.title: Proschi language reference
pages.description: The Proschi language at a glance: every statement with its syntax, a complete example, and links to the page that explains each part in detail.

pages.title: Nodes, groups and connections
pages.description: Declare nodes, groups and connections in Proschi: ids, display names, tech stacks from the catalog, replicas, owners and descriptions.

pages.title: Colors, legend and layout
pages.description: Style a Proschi diagram with colors, tags and a legend, steer the automatic layout with direction and rank, and see how canvas edits change the text.

pages.title: Use cases: request flows step by step
pages.description: Write Proschi use cases: request flows step by step, with endpoints, payloads, statuses, fan-out, and the reads and writes the simulation counts.

pages.title: Scenarios: success and failure paths
pages.description: Branch a Proschi use case into scenarios with alt: the success path and every way it fails, side by side, plus parallel steps and endpoint groups.

pages.title: Imports: split a design across files
pages.description: Split a Proschi design across files with import: the project root, remote sources, syncing them into a lock file, the security model and errors.

pages.title: Org diagrams and team systems
pages.description: Draw each team's design as one box, connect the teams, and let the simulation say which team cannot take the traffic you send to it.

pages.title: High-level design: traffic and capacity
pages.description: Add a high-level design to a Proschi diagram: quantities, traffic, capacity per node, the data model and decisions, all checked by the simulation.

pages.title: Requirements and tests for designs
pages.description: Check a Proschi design with requirements and tests: latency, availability, cost and survival limits, assertions on request flows, and selectors.

pages.title: Proschi grammar (EBNF)
pages.description: The complete Proschi grammar in EBNF: every statement, block, arrow and payload rule of the language on one page, for tool builders and quick lookups.

pages.title: How the simulation works
pages.description: What Proschi's simulation models (load, reads and writes, replicas and shards, queueing, percentiles, availability, cost), what it leaves out, and how far to trust its numbers.

pages.title: Editor support
pages.description: Proschi in VS Code, IntelliJ, Neovim, Helix and Sublime Text, on the command line and in CI: checking, formatting, OpenAPI, rendering and tests.

pages.title: Sharing and embedding
pages.description: Share a Proschi diagram as a link, as a short link with a preview image, or embed it read-only in a blog post, a wiki or docs with an iframe or oEmbed.

pages.title: Agent skills
pages.description: Skills for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot and Gemini CLI that turn docs, Terraform, Kubernetes, docker-compose and code into checked Proschi diagrams.

pages.title: Numbers to know
pages.description: Numbers every engineer should know for system design: latency, throughput, conversions, availability nines, object sizes, cloud costs and a worked estimate.

pages.title: Writing practice problems
pages.description: How a Proschi practice problem is put together: the statement, the given design, the reference solution, the wrong designs and the calibration.

pages.title: Writing practice cards
pages.description: How Proschi's practice cards are written: flip, choice, estimate and cloze cards, topics, ids that never change, and the check that catches duplicates.

pages.title: Writing game scenarios
pages.description: How Scale or Fail, Proschi's system design game, works on top of the simulation, and how to write its scenarios, tech cards and incidents, with reference runs that prove them.

pages.title: Privacy
pages.description: What Proschi keeps in your browser, what an account stores on the server, what is logged and shared, and how to export or delete it.
